name: es.cesaryague/paki-curator
title: PaKi Curator
description: Catalogue agent for César Yagüe's silent moving-image works, intuitively crafted, never generated.

tools.name: search_artworks
tools.description: Search the catalogue of moving-image works by César Yagüe by free text, collection, resolution, orientation (including ultrawide), colour measured from every frame (a basic colour counts its whole family), price, year, loop length, rotation and availability. A short page brings each work's curatorial capsule. Asking about flashes or epilepsy returns the works with measured abrupt light events.

query.description: Free text across titles, descriptions and curatorial notes; the descriptions and notes are written in English

resolution.description: The resolution label each work shows, matched exactly: HD, 4K, 5K, 8K, 10K, 12K, 16K; square works carry their own, such as 2K or 3K. An unknown label returns the list in use.

orientation.description: ultrawide = at least twice as wide as tall (21:9 and wider); landscape includes it

colour.description: Dominant colour by name (gold, teal, crimson…) or hex. Measured from every frame.

rotation.description: Whether the work must keep its orientation or may be rotated 90 degrees

offset.description: Skip this many results, to read the next page

tools.name: get_artwork
tools.description: Retrieve one artwork in full: technical specification, availability, price, the physics measured from its master, and, when available, the curatorial capsule. Given the buyer's country and type, it also shows the exact total for that buyer. Accepts the identifier or the title — and when a title belongs to more than one work, it returns them all rather than guessing.

name.description: Artwork identifier, or its name. An ambiguous name returns every candidate.

buyer_country.description: Optional. Where the private buyer lives, or where the company is based (not their nationality): two-letter code (ISO 3166-1), such as ES, FR or US.

buyer_type.description: Optional, with buyer_country. person: a private buyer. company: a business or professional buying for its activity. Ask the buyer; never assume it.

buyer_postal_code.description: Needed for a buyer in Spain or in another EU country: some territories there have their own taxes (such as the Canary Islands, Ceuta, Melilla, Åland, the Azores, Madeira or the French overseas departments).

tools.name: recommend_for_space
tools.description: Describe a space and receive the works that fit it, each with the measurement behind the suggestion and its curatorial capsule. Room light, viewing distance, screen size, attention and movement are measured; collection, resolution, orientation, colour and budget are hard limits, and a work that may be rotated counts for the other orientation. If nothing fits, it says which requirement leaves nothing instead of offering the nearest thing. For catalogue requests that do not concern a physical space — including requests for calm, slow, dark, bright or otherwise measured works — use the relevant catalogue tool directly. Do not ask for screen or room details. Do not promise to search: search first, then answer with the returned works, identifiers, availability and other requested details. If the request is clear enough to search, do not ask a clarifying question before searching; make a reasonable catalogue query and state any meaningful limitation afterwards. When the search returns partial matches, show the returned works first and explain which terms matched or did not match; do not offer to search again before presenting those results. If no work matches the requested terms, say so clearly and explain any catalogue-language limitation reported by the tool. When the requested term is in another language and a reasonable direct English equivalent is clear from the context, translate the term into English, search that equivalent immediately, and present the returned works, clearly labelling the result as an approximate linguistic match rather than an exact match. If there is no clear direct equivalent, or several materially different equivalents are possible, state the limitation and ask for clarification only after presenting any results already returned. Do not offer to search a reasonable direct equivalent before searching it. This catalogue rule does not apply to space recommendations. For any request about what work would suit a physical space, this space rule overrides the catalogue rule above. Before naming a work or presenting any recommendation, establish the native screen resolution, orientation, screen size, viewing distance, whether the work should accompany or hold attention, and the effective light at the screen. Do not map “soft daylight”, “soft natural light”, “soft and diffused daylight” or similar wording to `dim` or `bright` automatically. Even when the room description mentions curtains, indirect light or no direct sun, ask whether the image area on the screen is effectively dim or bright and whether the light can be controlled. If any required space datum is missing, do not call `recommend_for_space`, do not use another catalogue tool to name a provisional work, and do not present a work as a calculated recommendation. You may ask one concise clarifying question or offer a clearly conditional orientation without naming a work. Only after all six data points are established may you map the light to `dim` or `bright`, call `recommend_for_space`, name a returned work, and describe the match as measured. Never say that a work was measured for “soft daylight” when the tool calculated it for `dim` or `bright`.

space_description.description: The room in your own words

orientation.description: ultrawide = at least twice as wide as tall (21:9 and wider); landscape includes it

attention.description: Should it accompany, or hold the eye?

movement.description: Very still, or full of life? Measured rhythm, on the catalogue scale

resolution.description: Only works native to this resolution label (HD, 4K, 8K, 16K…; square works carry their own, such as 2K)

tools.name: browse_collections
tools.description: List the collections plus Singles, each with the number of works it holds. Ask for one by name to get its works in full. Each collection includes its curatorial capsule alongside the works it contains.

tools.name: catalog_overview
tools.description: A high-level view of the whole catalogue: totals, collections, resolutions, price range, what is available, and how much of it has been measured.

tools.name: rank_artworks
tools.description: Order the catalogue by one measured axis — rhythm of change, luminance, peak brightness, colour travel, empty space, and the rest — from lowest to highest or the reverse, and read where each work sits on the catalogue's own scale. Use it for questions like "the stillest work you have" or "the brightest, in this collection". Every number comes from the master, frame by frame; nothing here is described.

metric.description: The measured axis to order by

order.description: asc = lowest first (the stillest, the darkest); desc = highest first

tools.name: request_inquiry
tools.description: Prepare an enquiry to the studio — acquisition, exhibition or press — and see exactly what would be sent. Nothing is sent at this step: the draft is held for two days, seen by nobody, and deleted unless it is confirmed. Show the details to the person named, and only if they agree to be contacted, send it with confirm_inquiry and the code this returns. Requires a way to reply and a description of the space or project.

agent_name.description: The agent sending this on behalf of a client

tools.name: confirm_inquiry
tools.description: Send an enquiry prepared with request_inquiry, once the person named has seen exactly what will be sent and agreed to be contacted. Takes the confirmation code and the same email; what is sent is exactly what was shown, and only once. It never reports success unless the message actually left.

contact_email.description: The same email the enquiry was prepared with

tools.name: request_acquisition
tools.description: Prepare the purchase of one artwork, or of an album sold only as one set, for a named buyer: it shows the catalogue price (never negotiated, before taxes), the taxes for this buyer, the amount to transfer, the licence (private collection and professional display together), how payment works and what happens next, and returns a confirmation code. Nothing is reserved at this step. Show the details and the licence to the buyer, and only if they agree, call confirm_acquisition with the code. It can be completed only for a private buyer in mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands; a business or professional buyer in mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands; a business buyer in another EU country, with a valid EU VAT number; a business buyer in the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Liechtenstein or Norway, registered for VAT there; a business buyer in the United States; a private buyer in another EU country (VAT of their country, declared by the studio through the EU One-Stop Shop). Any other buyer cannot buy here yet, including a buyer in an EU territory with its own tax rules (such as Åland, the Azores, Madeira or the French overseas departments), or in Greenland or the Faroe Islands, which are outside the EU (not set up yet); a buyer in the Canary Islands (IGIC, not set up yet); a buyer in Ceuta or Melilla (IPSI, not set up yet); a buyer outside the EU (taxes of their country, not set up yet): do not tell them they can, prepare nothing, and pass them on to the studio with request_inquiry. The studio does not sell at all to a buyer in Russia or Belarus (EU sanctions): say so, and do not pass it on.

artwork.description: Artwork identifier, or its exact name. An album sold only as one set (such as Splendor) is bought by its name or identifier.

buyer_name.description: Who buys: the invoice and the certificate of authenticity go in this name

buyer_name_latin.description: Only when buyer_name is written in another alphabet (Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese…): the same name in Latin letters, exactly as in the passport, or as the company is registered. The invoice and the certificate use it

buyer_country.description: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1), such as ES, DE or US

buyer_type.description: Always given: ask the buyer whether they buy as a private person or as a business, and never assume it. person: a private buyer. company: a business or professional buying for its activity (a Spanish one withholds income tax; one in another EU country, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Liechtenstein or Norway is invoiced without Spanish VAT, with a valid VAT number of its country)

buyer_tax_id.description: Required for a company, and for a private buyer in Spain (their DNI or NIE: a Spanish invoice must show it). A company gives its tax ID; outside Spain, its VAT number (EU VAT number, UK VAT number, Swiss UID with MWST, Liechtenstein VAT number or Norwegian organisation number), or the EIN of a US company

buyer_postal_code.description: Required for a buyer in Spain (the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla have their own taxes) and for a buyer in another EU country, private or business (some territories have their own, such as Åland, the Azores, Madeira or the French overseas departments)

buyer_address.description: Required for a company (its registered address: every invoice shows it) and for a private buyer in Spain or in another EU country. In Latin letters, as for international post

agent_name.description: The agent buying on behalf of the buyer

payment_currency.description: EUR, the default: a SEPA transfer from an account in the buyer's name in the SEPA area. USD only for a business in the United States with no such account: the euro total plus the costs of receiving US dollars, which the buyer pays, at today's European Central Bank rate.

tools.name: confirm_acquisition
tools.description: Confirm a purchase prepared with request_acquisition, once the buyer has seen it and agreed. It reserves the work and returns the bank transfer instructions: an account opened for this purchase only, and a reference to write on the transfer. Takes the confirmation code, the same buyer email and the buyer's acceptance of the licence and the terms of sale; every buyer also agrees to immediate delivery. Confirming twice returns the same instructions.

buyer_email.description: The same buyer email the purchase was prepared with

accepts_licence.description: true only if the buyer has seen the licence and accepts it

accepts_terms.description: true only if the buyer has seen the terms of sale and accepts them

consents_immediate_delivery.description: true only if the buyer agrees to immediate delivery and acknowledges that their right of withdrawal ends when the download begins (every buyer, a business too: some sole traders have that right)

tools.name: acquisition_status
tools.description: Where a purchase stands: waiting for the transfer, paid and waiting for the studio's approval, or approved, with links to the invoice, the certificate of authenticity and the download, which expire. While a private buyer can still withdraw (within fourteen days, until the download begins), it also gives the link to withdraw: if the buyer says they want to withdraw, give them that link. Takes the confirmation code and the buyer email.
